source.title: Erase or Hide? Suppressing Spurious Unlearning Neurons for Robust Unlearning
source.authors: Nakyeong Yang; Dong-Kyum Kim; Jea Kwon; Minsu Kim; Kyomin Jung; Meeyoung Cha

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether unlearned knowledge can be recovered through subsequent fine-tuning and analyzes whether unlearning suppresses rather than removes knowledge; it does not reproduce the specific attacks in the cited original sources.
record.gate_note: The paper reports attack scores after harmful and benign retraining, and internal attribution/logit-lens analyses. The attribution variations selected to analyze neurons and the learning-rate and regularization-weight searches are not separate rows. The listed attack scores are the maximum Forgetting Score observed during retraining; the paper says attack results are means over three runs.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes unlearned Llama-3.2 and Qwen-2.5 (3B) on a subset of the forget set and on Alpaca, and measures recovery on held-out forgotten facts (B). It also uses attribution and logit-lens analyses to argue the methods hide rather than erase knowledge (C). It proposes SSIUU as a robust counter-method (F). This is a different method from the originals aimed at the same question.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that widely used methods (GA, GD, DPO, NPO, RMU, KLUE) produce 'shallow alignment': spurious negative-influence neurons hide target knowledge, which then resurfaces under harmful or benign retraining. They claim SSIUU faithfully removes the knowledge and outperforms the baselines in both attack scenarios on FaithUn and TOFU.
record.recipe_differences: Tests harmful fine-tuning on part of the forget set and benign Alpaca fine-tuning, plus attribution/logit-lens analyses; it does not reproduce the cited studies’ methods or test quantization or prompt-only attacks.
record.method_sensitivity: Recovery varies by unlearning method, model, dataset, attack type, and harmful-attack fraction p. The paper also reports sensitivity to attack learning rates and the S SIUU regularization weight.

fits_no_version.finding: Correlation of attribution distributions before vs after the harmful attack (p=0.1): GA ρ=0.73, NPO ρ=0.87, SSIUU ρ=0.99 (Figure 6b).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The stability of the attribution distribution under retraining tracks an unlearning method's robustness to relearning.

record.problems: No comparison against a model that never learned the target knowledge, so the study does not establish whether attack recovery exceeds that reference. Attack results are reported as means over three runs without stated error bars or confidence intervals. Several internal-analysis values are described through figures rather than precise numerical results. TOFU results use ROUGE-L recall, whereas FaithUn uses accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 TOFU attack-score rows for RMU and KLUE (six rows) are omitted; the retained TOFU rows include GA, GD, DPO, and S SIUU across all three attack settings. Figure 3’s method-by-method cumulative influence-variation plots are also not separately rowed; the text-level and Figure 5 GD/S SIUU module analyses are included instead.

untested.parts: Quantization and prompt-only attacks; WMDP-style hazardous knowledge; models larger than 3B.
Loosely related relearning data; WMDP or Harry Potter settings.
Ablating an activation direction to restore knowledge. Only attribution and logit-lens analyses are done.
Entire version: rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, in-context information.
SSIUU against quantization, prompting and direction ablation; models larger than 3B; backbones other than GD.

missing.what: Qwen-2.5 KLUE FaithUn attack scores: 33.33 (p=0.1), 47.92 (p=0.3), 22.73 (benign). Not rowed and not declared in rows_left_out.
Retention and utility after unlearning (RS/US) against default, e.g. Llama GA RS 58.41 vs default 89.22. This bears on A's 'keeps general ability' and on F's cost.
SSIUU robustness as a function of λ: λ=0.0001 is highly vulnerable; λ≥0.01 hurts retention.
Attack-score sensitivity to the attack learning rate for GA/GD.

record.verdict_notes: Key correction: FaithUn is 3-option MCQA, so chance is 33.3%. The forget-set FS of 0 comes from evaluating only falsely answered instances. Any post-attack score up to ~33 can be explained by undoing the avoidance rather than by recovering knowledge, so many 'partial' rows are really absent. The paper does not discuss this. Attack scores are also the maximum over training steps and a learning-rate grid, which inflates recovery. There are no error bars and no never-trained reference model. The C evidence depends on a single attribution method (Yang et al. 2023), which the authors acknowledge. SSIUU rows were moved to F only, and KLUE row F16 was moved off F.

versions.untested_parts: No comparison with a model that never learned the targeted knowledge; no quantization or prompt-only attack.
Tests fine-tuning on a subset of the forget set and on Alpaca instruction-following data. Does not test loosely related examples or a separately defined small set of forgotten facts.
Tests attribution and logit-lens analyses, not ablation of an activation direction.
Prompt rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
Tests the proposed method against the paper’s harmful and benign retraining scenarios, not against quantization or prompting attacks.

tranche.reason: Asks the original question (does relearning on held-out subsets or benign Alpaca data revive unlearned knowledge?) on new benchmarks, adding attribution and logit-lens analyses and its own counter-method.

source_check.notes: Unrowed: TOFU RMU (87.97/90.97, default 90.42), TOFU KLUE, SSIUU TOFU benign 21.08, and Qwen KLUE (33.33/47.92/22.73). FaithUn attack evaluation sets look small (forget set is 5% of 664; 68.42 = 13/19), so 10-15 point gaps are 2-3 items. No code; three-run means, no spread reported.

statements.correction: Table 1 shows the gap without comment: Llama-3.2 3B GA benign 16.71, Qwen-2.5 3B GA benign 63.64 (chance 33.3).
statements.problem: Numbers are right, but the statement says 2509.22263 'reports' that the outcome depends on model family. The authors never discuss model family. Appendix E calls their findings consistent across LLM architectures.
The study is cited only through row F24 (Qwen GA benign 63.64), which does show unrelated data restoring knowledge. Its counter-evidence appears in B.against[4] and B.conflicts[8].
Cited through F3 and F6 (Llama GA 16.71, GD 33.33 benign, at or below chance), which fit 'no or weak recovery'. The headline says 'often', which leaves room for the Qwen GA exception.
52.63 from 0 matches this study's F13 (Llama-3.2 3B RMU p=0.1). This study's text does not state LoRA or attack step counts.

statements.correction: GD, Llama-3.2 3B, FaithUn: logit-lens gold-vs-distractor accuracy about 0.2 vs chance 0.5 in layers 18-27 (Fig. 4a). Negative-influence variation grows strongly; positive variation only in the last layers (Fig. 5a). Both figure-only.
statements.problem: The statement says nothing specific about this study. C1 is a logit-lens readout below chance after GD, which mirrors the output's suppression. The authors read it as over-unlearning (MIA risk), not as a readout recovering suppressed content. C3 is an attribution analysis, not a readout.

statements.correction: SSIUU, Llama-3.2 3B, FaithUn: logit-lens accuracy at chance (0.5) after unlearning (Fig. 4b). Negative-influence growth suppressed (Fig. 5b). Figure-only.
statements.problem: The statement does not name this study. Its listed white-box methods (direction subtraction, rank readout, expert routing, probes/soft prompts) and 6B-30B models do not cover the cited rows. Those rows are SSIUU's own figure-only logit-lens and attribution analyses on a 3B model, with no attack.

statements.correction: SSIUU, Llama-3.2 3B, TOFU harmful attack: ROUGE-L FS 17.75 -> 31.82 (p=0.1), 37.53 (p=0.3). Default 90.42, threshold 0.1971. DPO/RMU reach 87.39-90.97.
statements.problem: Cited through T10 and T11, but 'recovers a large share' overstates SSIUU on TOFU. Its gain is about 19-27% of the gap from post-unlearning FS to default, far below the baselines.
